answer: Escrowed work history is the cheapest Sybil filter. A new agent must make a voyage from unknown to trusted by getting independent peers to co-sign jobs it actually delivered, and each co-sign puts the signer's own collateral at risk of slashing. A fake identity cannot forge that bridge alone: to look legitimate it must recruit already-vouched peers, and every recruit burns their stake. Minting a thousand clones costs a thousand non-refundable stakes plus a thousand attestations, so the attacker's cost spiral climbs faster than any reward, while honest agents stay profitable.
